parameters.name: uone
parameters.description: `uone = 60` U_1 is a round input scale chosen before fitting, comparable to the training input magnitude, solely for conditioning; it is not a fitted threshold.

parameters.name: utwo
parameters.description: `utwo = 20` U_2 is a round input scale chosen before fitting, comparable to the training input magnitude, solely for conditioning; it is not a fitted threshold.

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: `eps = 1e-10` is a dimensionless numerical lower guard for the logarithm, used in the fitting code to avoid invalid trial evaluations; chosen, not fitted, and inactive on the logged and final simulated trajectories.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Feedback magnitude, jointly fitted; see expression for whether it multiplies a state difference or a dimensionless logarithm.

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Dimensionless first-input feedback modifier or sigmoid location, as specified by the expression.

parameters.name: ybase
parameters.description: Fitted reference state, not assumed to be an independently measured physical equilibrium.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Magnitude of the second-input forcing at normalized input unity.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Dimensionless fitted exponent of the nonnegative normalized second input.

estimation.criterion: Minimize the unweighted sum of squared predicted-minus-logged `dy` residuals over both files. This directly uses the supplied derivative target and was selected over rollout-only and joint criteria by the internal suffix simulation comparison.
estimation.data: Final parameter estimation uses every derivative row of data/train.csv and data/val.csv as two separate trajectories. Where rollout residuals enter, it also uses all states after the first of each trajectory. Initial structural searches fitted data/train.csv only and compared free-running simulation on data/val.csv. A subsequent criterion comparison fitted the full training file plus zero-based validation rows 0 through 727 and evaluated rows 728 through 1453, with an independent measured initialization at row 728. The suffix was then included in the final refit to use all supplied identification information. No test data were accessed. No rows were discarded in the final fit.
estimation.method: The preliminary training derivative fit used bounded trust-region reflective nonlinear least squares, scipy.optimize.least_squares, from three deterministic numerical start vectors (`k = 0.14999999999999999`, `g = 0.55000000000000004`, `ybase = 1`, `source = 0.01`, `n = 2`); (`k = 0.10426776347397033`, `g = 0.37834063291241088`, `ybase = 1.0409574953531975`, `source = 0.011381957167595116`, `n = 2.5773222365091346`); (`k = 0.131600949125012`, `g = 0.55855513461419803`, `ybase = 0.83740432999593806`, `source = 0.0091553332644630624`, `n = 1.0882204604234511`). These were generated in the exploratory search with numpy random seed 15; the best derivative SSE solution initialized later fits. Bounds for the preliminary and final model were `k` in `[0.0001, 5]` U_y/s; `g` in `[-5, 5]` -; `ybase` in `[0.69999999999999996, 1.3]` U_y; `source` in `[0, 0.5]` U_y/s; `n` in `[0.20000000000000001, 8]` -. They are numerical identification constraints allowing broad reference states and positive source/exponent/rate, not supplied physical information. The final solution does not reach these bounds. The final solver starts were `k = 0.2403107786759682`, `g = 0.645895900326797`, `ybase = 0.99114930544043045`, `source = 0.014682642436529374`, `n = 1.4906345010506576`, taken from log_feedback derivative in nonlinear_results.json because the prior derivative fit was already in a reasonable local basin. Final and criterion-comparison fits use scipy.optimize.least_squares with trust-region reflective, `x_scale = "jac"`, maximum 800 function evaluations, and dimensionless tolerances `ftol = 1e-10`, `xtol = 1e-10`, `gtol = 1e-10`. Nonlinear least squares supports the free-running residual criterion, for which a linear coefficient solve is not available. No random numbers enter this final step. Criterion selection compared derivative-only least squares, rollout-only least squares, and joint least squares with derivative residuals multiplied by `10*sqrt(w)` s for dimensionless trial weights `w = 1` and `w = 10`. The 10 s residual scale is a chosen conditioning/tradeoff scale, not an identified time constant. The criterion with smallest suffix rollout RMSE was selected. Every rollout uses classical RK4 with 5 s steps, logged inputs held constant, and a single first-state initialization, never later measured-state resets. All fitted parameters are jointly reestimated at each fitting stage; intermediate estimates are not frozen.

discussion.family: Logarithmic nonlinear state-feedback model with affine input modulation and power-law input forcing. General nonlinear-model reference: O. Nelles, Nonlinear System Identification, Springer, 2001 (bibliographic reference recalled from memory, not externally checked).
discussion.interpretation: The state `y`, inputs `x1` and `x2`, and target `dy` are the logged columns. Their physical units are unknown. `U_y`, `U_1` and `U_2` below denote unspecified native units of `y`, `x1` and `x2`; `dy` has units `U_y/s`. In `-k*(1-g*(x1/uone))*log(Max(y/ybase,eps))+source*Max(x2/utwo,0)**n`, `log(Max(y/ybase,eps))` is a sublinear state deviation above the reference. The factor `1-g*(x1/uone)` changes feedback magnitude with the first input and may change its sign. The power term increases forcing with the second input, while `Max(x2/utwo,0)` extends the input response as zero below zero to avoid complex fractional powers. The guard is numerical, not an identified physical law.
discussion.origin: Strong fitted input-state interactions motivated affine input modulation rather than constant-rate relaxation. State-logarithm feedback was guessed as a compact sublinear alternative to state polynomials. Affine, logarithmic, rational, signed-power, hyperbolic-tangent and exponential feedback forms were compared; the logarithmic form improved validation over affine feedback using only five fitted parameters. No supplied physics selected the logarithm or power exponent. In the internal criterion comparison, the best suffix rollout RMSE was 0.051168782 U_y on rows 728 through 1453 of data/val.csv, initialized only at row 728 (zero-based rows). This suffix was excluded from that fitting stage but had already been inspected in exploratory validation, so this is not a pristine independent estimate. After refitting on both complete files, the training and validation rollout RMSE values are 0.033566678 and 0.039841839 U_y; these final values are in-sample, not unseen-data scores. Final predicted-minus-logged derivative residual lag-one correlations are 0.494632 and 0.467064 (dimensionless) on training and validation, respectively.
discussion.limitations: There is no supplied physical description or intended use; no term is assigned a physical mechanism. This is a scalar autonomous-in-state, memoryless-in-input approximation, not evidence that omitted dynamics are absent. It cannot represent input histories, disturbances or time-dependent hidden states. Observed derivative residual correlation motivated nonlinear feedback and input-rate interactions, but remained after these extensions. Sampled derivatives need not be exact continuous-time derivatives, and integration-method effects are absorbed into fitted values. Extrapolation beyond the sampled state/input ranges is unverified; uncertainty intervals were not estimated. Positive measured states support the logarithmic branch, not behavior near zero. The guard has no physical justification below its cutoff; input feedback can become amplifying at sufficiently high first input.
